redFlags.intro: Most days none of this will apply. It is here so you don't have to remember it when you feel rotten.

groups.title: Call 999 or go to A&E now
items: A sudden severe headache that reaches its worst within a minute.

groups.title: Same day — call 111 or ask for an urgent GP appointment
items: A headache that is clearly worse lying flat, or on coughing, straining or bending.
A fever with a stiff neck.
New loss of vision, or double vision.
A calf that is swollen, red or painful — with your medicines, clot symptoms need same-day advice.
A blood-pressure reading of 180/120 or higher.
A headache that feels genuinely different in character from your usual ones.

groups.title: GP soon — days, not weeks
items: Headaches on most days for weeks.
Any new breast change, either side.
New pelvic pain that doesn't settle.
Any thought of stopping a prescribed medicine — talk it through first, side effects can usually be managed.

checkBefore.title: The standing rule
paragraphs: Before any new tablet, remedy or supplement — even something picked up in a supermarket — tell the pharmacist about your breast-cancer medicine.
Pharmacy computer checks often miss things bought off the shelf, so saying it out loud is what makes the check work.
It takes one sentence at the counter, and it covers painkillers, cold remedies, sleep aids, herbal products and vitamins alike.
